body:
A part now reports to the orchestrator that launched it, on the computer that launched it, and its post says who that is. Taking over the board no longer steals or loses anyone's parts: a part changes hands only when an orchestrator claims it, or when its own orchestrator hands over on the same computer. A Done that cannot be delivered is written on the post, and every orchestrator sees it to claim.

### What changed
- **Launch records the owner.** `kit.py launch` writes on the post the launching orchestrator's address (its real session id: `session_…` on the web, the CLI session id on a computer), its session name (`<slug>-orchestrator` on a computer, what SendMessage takes) and its device (`web`, or the host name; `KIT_DEVICE` overrides).
- **Only a claim or a hand-over changes it.** `kit.py claim <post>` writes the claimer's address on the post (for the part and for its review), clears any `orchestrator_unreached`, and prints the line to send the part. `handover.py --role orchestrator` now writes `.kit/run/handover-from.json` (who is replaced, on which device); the successor's `resume --role orchestrator` inherits every open part the predecessor owned on that device, and never one of another device. The takeover line in the three orchestrator guides no longer says "tell each running session your id": it says a takeover claims nothing.
- **Resume says where to report.** `kit.py resume --role part` has a "Where you report" section: the owner, its device, how it got the step (launched or claimed), and how to reach exactly that session (send_message by id for a web one; on a computer, SendMessage to the name, only the row of the recorded device, never a look-alike). The part guides (agy, CLI, web) point to it instead of a fixed name.
- **A failed send is written.** `kit.py unreached <post> --why W` writes `orchestrator_unreached {at, to, device, why}` on the post; every orchestrator's resume lists those parts with the claim command.
- **Reviews and the clerk.** `kit.py review` fills `<ORCH_ID>` with the orchestrator launching it and records `review_orchestrator*` on the step; `resume --role review` prints the same "Where you report" (a claim overrides it). The CLI consultant guide no longer messages the fixed name. The CLI clerk messages the orchestrator on its own computer; `resume --role clerk` names the device.

### How it was checked
- tests/test_cl49_orchestrator_owner.py runs a real local board server: launch as the laptop orchestrator, then a web orchestrator writes its id on `_orchestrator` (the takeover), then the part's resume is read: it names `a1b2-laptop-orch` on `owners-laptop`, never the web session. Then claim, unreached (listed, then cleared by a claim), hand-over on the same device (inherited) and on another device (nothing inherited), the review prompt (its launcher, not `_orchestrator`), and the six guides (no fixed-name target).
- `breaks` removes the owner from the launch fields: the launch and takeover tests fail.

### Files
- scripts/kit.py (and its installed copy .kit/kit.py): `my_device`, `orchestrator_here`, `step_owner`, `report_lines`, `claim`, `unreached`, `unreached_lines`, `inherit_lines`; launch, review and the four resume roles.
- kit/handover.py: `record_predecessor`.
- kit/part.template.md, kit/claude-cli/part.template.md, kit/claude/part.template.md; the three consultant guides; kit/claude-cli/clerk.template.md; the three orchestrator guides.

task:
A part reports to the orchestrator that started it, on the device that started it, unless another orchestrator has claimed that part. CL44's part said Done and messaged `board-orchestrator`, the fixed name in the part guide (`{{SLUG}}-orchestrator`): it was launched by the orchestrator on the owner's computer (a Claude Code CLI session), and the name matched two dead sessions on another computer, last active 3 days ago. The Done never arrived. A web orchestrator had taken over the board meanwhile, but had not claimed CL44: CL44 still belonged to the orchestrator that launched it.

1. `kit.py launch` records on the post who owns the part: the launching orchestrator's session (its address) and its device (`orchestrator`, `orchestrator_device`).
2. The owner changes only by a claim: an orchestrator takes a part explicitly (`kit.py claim <post>`: it writes its own address on the post and tells the part), or a successor orchestrator on the same device, after a hand-over (session limit, reset), inherits every part its predecessor owned there. Taking over the board alone claims nothing.
3. `kit.py resume --role part` prints where to report: the post's owner now; the part guides use it instead of a fixed name, in kit/part.template.md and kit/claude-cli/part.template.md.
4. When the send fails or the owner names no live session, the part says so in its post (`orchestrator_unreached`), and every orchestrator's resume lists such parts so one can claim them.
5. The same rule for reviews and the clerk: their guides also message the fixed `{{SLUG}}-orchestrator` (M1's review finished and its message went to the same dead sessions); they report to the orchestrator that launched them, unless another claimed the step.
title: A part reports to the orchestrator that started it, unless another claimed it
verdict: CL44's case is replayed and fixed: the part names its launcher on the laptop, not the web orchestrator nor a look-alike name; claim, hand-over and failed sends are recorded on the post.
